**Finding: Deviation (medium) — Warranty and duration, §§ 5.1 / 5.4**

**What the document does today**
- § 5.1(a) gives only a "reasonable care and skill" services standard (with a professional-custom gloss) plus a personnel commitment; § 5.1(b) is corporate authority; the closing covenant is limited to "laws applicable to IBM's business."
- There is **no conformance warranty** for Materials/deliverables, **no warranty period**, and **no remedy** (no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund).
- No malicious-code warranty.
- § 5.4(c) provides **all Materials "AS IS", without warranty of any kind**, which largely swallows the express commitment — close to the playbook walk-away position. §§ 5.4(a)–(b) and 5.3(b) add further disclaimers (no error-free operation, no capacity/performance/scalability, no secure operation).
- § 5.2 exclusivity is acceptable in itself, since it preserves § 5.1.

**Redline submitted (validated ok:true)**
1. Insert after p0062 — new § 5.1(c)/(d): 90-day conformance-to-documentation warranty for each Material/deliverable; no malicious code introduced by IBM; and an express remedy at IBM's option of re-performance, repair/replacement, or refund of fees paid for the non-conforming item.
2. Amend § 5.4(c) (p0074) — prefix "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1," so the "AS IS" disclaimer no longer overrides the express warranty.

**Fallback offered in the comment:** 30 days for Services if 90 is resisted, but a conformance warranty with a real remedy for deliverables is not waivable.
